comments.body:
@pcbeingused333 is attempting to deploy a commit to the **Callstack** Team on [Vercel](https://vercel.com).

A member of the Team first needs to [authorize it](https://vercel.com/git/authorize?team=Callstack&slug=callstack-team&teamId=team_jILdbx4rO9xVffZRmhpF5qU1&type=github&job=%7B%22headInfo%22%3A%7B%22sha%22%3A%2213f2392a0af42735a452370c70cb6ec04533b389%22%7D%2C%22id%22%3A%22QmWe4a9CeG2d3Yae5tidAnfPU1ayjMLnAFHCDBz8zkLGpa%22%2C%22org%22%3A%22callstack%22%2C%22prId%22%3A4123%2C%22repo%22%3A%22agent-device%22%7D).

The change looks right in code at 13f2392, but it needs live device evidence before merge.

The guard changes when alert reads reach the iOS XCTest runner on the `open --launch-url` route (3000 ms window), which is a device-facing dispatch change ([alert.ts#L109](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/13f2392/packages/platform-apple/src/alert.ts#L109)). The fake-timer tests with a mocked runner cannot show that the runner stops hitting its main-thread timeout and that the probe stops reporting `alert-read`. The failure was intermittent (seen twice on iPhone 17e, iOS 27.0), so mocks cannot confirm it is gone. Please run `open <app> --launch-url <url whose scheme the app owns>` on an iOS simulator where no "Open in" prompt appears, about 10 times to cover the last-poll window. In every run, `launchConfirmationProbeFailure` must be absent, `launchConfirmation` must be undefined, and there must be no alert-read warning. Also run `alert wait --timeout 3000` on a quiet screen. It must end with the typed "alert wait timed out" absence (`ALERT_NOT_FOUND`), not a main-thread timeout. Record the device, source SHA and commands in the PR, or say there was no device available.

Not blocking, take or leave: the last read now starts about 500-800 ms before the end of the window, so `awaitAppleAlert` can finish roughly 2.5 s into a 3 s wait and miss an alert that appears in that tail (fine to accept, but worth a line in the PR body or `alert wait` docs); `MIN_ALERT_READ_BUDGET_MS` could live next to the other alert budgets in `alert-contract.ts`; the loop now has two budget checks plus a clock re-read, which one `nextReadBudgetMs(start, windowMs): number | undefined` could replace; and the new tests sit between the "whole point of typing absence" comment and the three tests it describes.

The two open inline threads still apply: the [`budgets.slice(1)` test shape](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374442) is a non-blocking nit, so assert `budgets.length >= 2` first, as the wait test does. The [macOS `timeoutMs` thread](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374450) does not apply: the guard targets the iOS runner's main-thread timeout, which has no macOS helper equivalent, and bounding macOS helper reads is a separate gap. Please resolve it as out of scope.

The only failing check is the Vercel deploy authorization for the fork. It builds the website and does not touch this code, so it is likely unrelated. No other check ran on this head, so the test and gate lanes have not run, and the lint, format, tsc and test results in the PR body are unconfirmed. I did not run the unit tests, and I confirmed the red-before-fix claim only by replaying the budget arithmetic against the old loop. Before merge, the live simulator evidence above is needed, and a maintainer must authorize the real CI lanes for this fork head.

Thanks for the detailed steps. I don't have access to macOS or an iOS simulator, so I can't produce that live evidence. I'll leave the code here as is: if someone on your side with a simulator can run the check, the change is ready; otherwise feel free to close it.

Thanks, that makes sense. Nothing more is needed from you here. The code at 13f2392 still reads right to me, and the remaining step is a maintainer run of `open --launch-url` on an iOS simulator to confirm the alert read no longer times out, which we will pick up on our side.
This conflicts with main now. Please rebase it so the remaining maintainer simulator run can happen on the rebased head.

Rebased onto current main. Since #4187 already covers the wait path (`awaitAppleAlert`), this PR now keeps only the matching gap in `actOnAppleAlert`: no further runner read is started when the remaining budget is below 500 ms. The title and description are updated to match (now `Refs #4018` instead of `Fixes`).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks for the rebase. At f104c7d the conflict is gone and CI is green. Since #4187 covers the `open --launch-url` wait route, what remains is the guard in [`alert.ts`](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f104c7d/packages/platform-apple/src/alert.ts#L156): `alert accept` and `alert dismiss` no longer send the last retry in the 2 s window when under 500 ms remain. The code reads correctly. The open item is live evidence for this device-facing change: the only test mocks `runAppleRunnerCommand` with fake timers, and the hosted Apple device lanes do not run for fork PRs, so we do not yet know how the runner answers a short-deadline alert command or whether the guard drops an alert that appears in the last 500 ms.

A maintainer iOS simulator run at f104c7d is the next step. In a quiet app with no alert, run `alert accept` and `alert dismiss` about 10 times each; every run should end with `ALERT_NOT_FOUND` and the scoped-snapshot hint (not `ALERT_UNRESOLVED` or `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT`), and the runner log should show each alert command's `timeoutMs` at 500 or more. Then trigger a permission alert about 1 s after the command starts; `alert accept` must still accept it. The same loop on `main` would show whether the late-retry failure reproduces on this route.

Could the guard reuse the rule #4187 added? In [`awaitAppleAlert`](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/f104c7d/packages/platform-apple/src/alert.ts#L166) a read is skipped when `remainingMs <= ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (300 ms). The act loop could do the same after its sleep, which removes `MIN_ALERT_READ_BUDGET_MS` and `canHoldRead`. If the live run shows 300 ms is not enough for the act route, one named floor in `alert-contract.ts` could serve both loops; today the same runner command gets two different minimum budgets with no recorded reason.

Not blocking, take or leave: add `assert.ok(budgets.length >= 2)` in `alert.test.ts`, so the `budgets.slice(1)` check cannot pass when the act loop never retries. That is also what the [open test thread](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374442) asks. The [macOS `timeoutMs` thread](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374450) does not apply: the guard only decides whether a retry starts, and macOS has no runner main-thread timeout to avoid, so it can be resolved.

Thanks for the update. The code at eacd5a8 now fixes the earlier test gap: alert.test.ts now asserts `budgets.length >= 2` before it checks each retry budget. The change itself looks right, but it is not ready to merge yet, because there is no live device run for the new guard.

The one reported check passes. The hosted Apple device lanes did not run for this fork PR, so CI does not exercise the runner alert route that this guard changes.

Before merge, please run `alert accept` and `alert dismiss` on an iOS simulator at eacd5a8 (`pnpm build`, `pnpm build:xcuitest`, `pnpm clean:daemon`) on the XCTest runner route. In a quiet app with no alert, about 10 runs of each must end with ALERT_NOT_FOUND and the scoped-snapshot hint, never ALERT_UNRESOLVED or MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT. The runner log must show every alert command with timeoutMs above 300, and no read started in the last 300 ms. Then trigger a permission alert about 1 s after the command starts, and confirm it is still accepted. Please record the device, source SHA and commands in the PR. Running the first check on main as well would show that the late-retry failure reproduces.

On the open threads: the P1 thread on the retry floor (https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4487115299) still applies. A retry can start with 301-499 ms left. That matches the floor used by awaitAppleAlert, so the live run above decides whether 301 ms is enough. If it is not, please raise one named floor in alert-contract.ts for both loops. Two threads can be resolved. The macOS timeout thread (https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374450) does not apply: the guard only decides whether another retry starts, and the dropped per-call timeout is already on main and out of scope. The thread on the retry count assertion (https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#discussion_r4432374442) is fixed at this head.

Not blocking, take or leave: alert.test.ts:172 asserts the literal 300, so importing ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS from @agent-device/contracts/alert-contract and asserting `budget > ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` would keep it in step with the contract. The PR body also still describes the old `MIN_ALERT_READ_BUDGET_MS` 500 ms design, so the Fix and Tests sections could say that a retry starts only with more than 300 ms left.

Earlier review: https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4123#issuecomment-6647283816

Live run at eacd5a8 on iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0 (Xcode 27.1), XCTest runner route. Built with `pnpm build` and `pnpm build:xcuitest`, fresh daemon in a private state dir. Control: `origin/main` at c96a2d5, built the same way, own state dir.

**1. Quiet app, no alert (Settings open), 10× `alert accept` + 10× `alert dismiss`**

`agent-device alert accept|dismiss --json --platform ios --udid <udid> --session <s>`

- eacd5a8: 20/20 ended `ALERT_NOT_FOUND`, with hint "If the permission sheet is visible in snapshot or screenshot but alert reports no alert, take a scoped snapshot around the visible button label and use press @ref." No `ALERT_UNRESOLVED`, no `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT`. Each run made 4 runner reads in ~1.75 s. One run made a 5th read.
- main: 20/20 ended `ALERT_NOT_FOUND` with the same hint. But every run made a 5th read with only ~215-293 ms left.

**2. Read budgets (timeoutMs)**

The runner log does not print `timeoutMs`. It logs only `COMMAND_ACCEPTED command=alert commandId=...`. So I worked out each read's budget from the request log: 2000 ms minus the time between request start and each `ios_runner_command_send`. Request start is a little before the retry loop starts, so these numbers are a lower bound.

- eacd5a8, 61 retry reads: budgets ~1480-1570, ~1025-1150, ~590-725 ms. The single 5th read started at 1700 ms (budget ≈300 ms by this lower bound, so just above 300 ms by the guard). It returned `ALERT_NOT_FOUND` in 119 ms. No read started with clearly ≤300 ms left.
- main: every run started a read in the last 300 ms (≈215-293 ms left). The failure reproduces on main in a quiet screen: 3 of 34 quiet calls ended `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT`. Example: a 6th read started at 1969 ms with ≈31 ms left. The runner logged `MAIN_THREAD_WORK_ABANDONED operation=command_execution slice=0.0` and the command ended `MAIN_THREAD_TIMEOUT` with no alert on screen. Two more the same way, with a 6th read at 2003-2004 ms.

**3. Real permission alert that appears about 1 s after the command starts**

Safari page on localhost that calls `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition` when the host signals it. A new origin (port) for each run, so a fresh "“localhost” Would Like to Use Your Location" prompt appears 1.0-1.3 s after the daemon request starts.
